caveats: Shares are not dollar loss, exposure duration, recovery cost or probabilities.
Validation groups were already used for other research; no independent claim follows.
Zero-heavy targets can improve squared-error metrics while worsening aggregate absolute error.
Final tests remain unopened, and severity models cannot enter probability gates.
Synthetic hypothetical fills only; no public execution calibration.
interpretation: Validation RMSE was 3.7277 shares for ridge and 3.6679/3.6605 for two neural seeds, versus 4.0826 zero and 3.9122 train-mean controls. Neural mean improvement over ridge, 0.0635 shares, missed the preregistered 0.10 threshold, so ridge is selected. Aggregate MAE was worse than the zero control and positive-outcome MAE remained about 9 shares. These expected-value fits provide limited information about individual severe events.
next_experiment: Study positive-outcome uncertainty and hurdle/quantile baselines before any severity-based policy. Continue genuine economic-regime reruns without retuning existing opened final tests.
title: Severity fits modestly reduce RMSE but retain large positive-outcome errors
